title: Minimal polynomial and maximal-fibre formula over a Tate algebra
statement:
Let $K$ be a complete field [def-weil-field] with a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value, and let $d\ge0$ and $T=K\langle U_1,\ldots,U_d\rangle$ be the restricted-series ring [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation]. Let $C\ne0$ be an affinoid $K$-algebra and let $j:T\hookrightarrow C$ be an injective $K$-algebra homomorphism making $C$ a finitely generated $T$-module. Suppose $C$ is torsion-free over $T$: for $t\in T\setminus\{0\}$, $j(t)c=0$ implies $c=0$. For each $c\in C$ there is a unique monic polynomial $p_c(Z)=Z^r+\sum_{i=1}^r t_iZ^{r-i}\in T[Z]$, of degree $r\ge1$, whose principal ideal equals the kernel of evaluation $T[Z]\to C$, $Z\mapsto c$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset T$, the set $Y_{\mathfrak m}=\{\mathfrak n\in\operatorname{Max}C:j^{-1}(\mathfrak n)=\mathfrak m\}$ is finite and nonempty, and
$$\max_{\mathfrak n\in Y_{\mathfrak m}}|c\bmod\mathfrak n|=\max_{1\le i\le r}|t_i\bmod\mathfrak m|^{1/i}.$$
The absolute values on these finite residue fields are the unique extensions of that on $K$ [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus]. Neither $C$ being reduced nor $c$ being separable is assumed.

source.place: Section 1.4, Lemma 12(i)-(ii), printed pp.25-27; primary PDF read online 2026-10-24, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-tate-integrally-closed], $T$ is an integrally closed domain. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], choose a monic $h\in T[Z]$ with $h(c)=0$. Put $F=\operatorname{Frac}(T)$ and $D=(T\setminus\{0\})^{-1}C$. The map $C\to D$ is injective: $c/1=0$ means $tc=0$ for some nonzero $t\in T$, so torsion-freeness gives $c=0$. The same argument makes $F\to D$ injective. Among nonzero annihilators of $c/1$ in $F[Z]$, take one of least degree and divide by its leading coefficient to obtain a monic $p_F$. Its degree $r$ is positive because $D\ne0$. Long division over $F$ shows that it divides every annihilator: the remainder also vanishes and has smaller degree. Thus $p_F\mid h_F$. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-monic-divisor-descent] to $T,F,h,p_F$ to obtain $p\in T[Z]$ mapping to $p_F$. Injectivity $T\to F$ makes $p$ monic of degree $r$, and injectivity $C\to D$ gives $p(c)=0$.

source.place: Section 1.4 Lemma 12(i)-(ii), printed pp.26-27 (PDF pp.27-28); primary PDF read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Divide any $g\in T[Z]$ with $g(c)=0$ by the monic $p$: cancelling its leading term repeatedly gives $g=qp+v$ with $\deg v<r$. Then $v(c)=0$. Its image in $F[Z]$ is a lower-degree annihilator, hence zero by the preceding minimality, so coefficient injectivity gives $v=0$. Conversely every multiple of $p$ vanishes. Hence the evaluation kernel is $(p)$. Any other monic generator divides $p$ and is divided by $p$; degrees add over the domain $T$, so both quotients are constants, and comparison of leading coefficients makes them $1$. This proves uniqueness. Write $p=Z^r+\sum_{i=1}^r t_iZ^{r-i}$ and set $A=T[c]\subset C$. Evaluation induces the explicit isomorphism $T[Z]/(p)\to A$, sending $[g]$ to $g(c)$; surjectivity is the definition of $A$ and injectivity is the kernel equality just proved.

source.place: Section 1.4 Lemma 12(i)-(ii), printed pp.26-27 (PDF pp.27-28); primary PDF read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak m\in\operatorname{Max}T$ and put $k=T/\mathfrak m$. Since $C$ is a finite $T$-module, $T\subset C$ is integral by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]; [pqf-lem-lying-over] lifts $\mathfrak m$ to a prime of $C$, and [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal] makes this lift maximal. Thus $Y_{\mathfrak m}$ is nonempty. If $e_1,\ldots,e_N$ span $C$ over $T$, their residues span $C/\mathfrak m C$ over $k$. This finite-dimensional commutative $k$-algebra is Artinian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dim-algebra-artinian] and has finite spectrum by [lem-sfb-artinian-spectrum-finite]. Its maximal ideals correspond to $Y_{\mathfrak m}$ by inverse image under the quotient map. Indeed a maximal ideal containing $\mathfrak m C$ contracts to a proper ideal containing the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, hence contracts to $\mathfrak m$. Therefore $Y_{\mathfrak m}$ is finite. By [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus], $k$ and every $C/\mathfrak n$ are finite field extensions of $K$ with unique extending absolute values.

source.place: Section 1.4 Lemma 12(i)-(ii), printed pp.26-27 (PDF pp.27-28); primary PDF read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $K$ by [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique]. Since $k/K$ is finite, embed $k$ in $\Omega$ over $K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-extension-embeds-algebraically-closed]. Give $\Omega$ the multiplicative nonarchimedean extending norm from [lem-trf-spectral-norm-algebraic-extension]. By [lem-sfb-algebraic-absolute-value-unique], its restriction to $k$ agrees with the residue absolute value. Let $\bar p\in k[Z]$ be the reduction of $p$. Its leading coefficient remains $1$, so its degree is $r\ge1$. Over $\Omega$ it factors into $r$ monic linear factors: repeatedly take a root using algebraic closedness and divide by $Z-\alpha$, decreasing degree until the monic constant $1$ remains. Keep repetitions in this list of roots.

source.place: Section 1.4 Lemma 12(i)-(ii), printed pp.26-27 (PDF pp.27-28); primary PDF read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: The same $T$-module generators of $C$ span it over $A=T[c]$, so $A\subset C$ is finite and hence integral by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. A root $\alpha\in\Omega$ of $\bar p$ defines $A\simeq T[Z]/(p)\to\Omega$ by $[g]\mapsto\bar g(\alpha)$. Its image is $k[\alpha]$, a finite-dimensional domain over $k$, hence a field: multiplication by a nonzero element is injective and therefore surjective. Its kernel $\mathfrak q$ is maximal and contracts to $\mathfrak m$. Apply [pqf-lem-lying-over] to the injection $A\subset C$, obtaining a prime $\mathfrak n$ contracting to $\mathfrak q$; [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal] makes it maximal. It lies in $Y_{\mathfrak m}$. The inclusion $A/\mathfrak q\hookrightarrow C/\mathfrak n$ sends the residue of $c$ to that of $c$. Pulling the absolute value of $\Omega$ back to $A/\mathfrak q\simeq k[\alpha]$, and restricting the absolute value of $C/\mathfrak n$ to that field, gives two absolute values extending that of $K$. They agree by [lem-sfb-algebraic-absolute-value-unique], so $|\alpha|=|c\bmod\mathfrak n|$. Lying-over was applied before taking the quotient; no injection after reduction is asserted.

source.place: Section 1.4 Lemma 12(i)-(ii), printed pp.26-27 (PDF pp.27-28); primary PDF read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Conversely, for any $\mathfrak n\in Y_{\mathfrak m}$, the embedding $k\hookrightarrow C/\mathfrak n$ is induced by $T\to C$. The extension $C/\mathfrak n$ is algebraic over $k$ (it is finite over $K$). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-extension-embeds-algebraically-closed] to extend our chosen embedding $k\to\Omega$ to $C/\mathfrak n\to\Omega$. The image $\beta$ of $c\bmod\mathfrak n$ satisfies $\bar p(\beta)=0$, since $p(c)=0$. Uniqueness [lem-sfb-algebraic-absolute-value-unique], now on $C/\mathfrak n$ over $K$, shows $|\beta|=|c\bmod\mathfrak n|$. Thus the set of absolute values of roots of $\bar p$ is exactly the set of fibre values $|c\bmod\mathfrak n|$; roots and maximal ideals need not be in bijection, and multiplicities do not affect maxima.

source.place: Section 1.4 Lemma 12(i)-(ii), printed pp.26-27 (PDF pp.27-28); primary PDF read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-tate-root-spectral-formula] with base field $k$, extension field $\Omega$, the restriction of its multiplicative nonarchimedean norm, and the linear factorization of $\bar p$ from step 4. It gives the maximum root norm as $\max_{0\le j<r}|\bar p_j|^{1/(r-j)}$. Substitute $j=r-i$; then $\bar p_{r-i}=t_i\bmod\mathfrak m$. Steps 5 and 6 identify the maximum root norm with $\max_{\mathfrak n\in Y_{\mathfrak m}}|c\bmod\mathfrak n|$, proving the formula. Both maxima are over finite nonempty sets. Repeated factors, inseparable roots and nilpotents in $C$ have not been discarded at any stage, and the argument also includes $d=0$ and $c=0$.

split_report.summary: Statement unchanged. Expanded Bosch Lemma 12(i)-(ii) into seven steps, preserving the monic evaluation-kernel construction and using lying-over on T[c]⊂C before reduction. Cited the existing lem-trf-tate-integrally-closed for normality of T (reviewer FIX: the delivered factoriality node duplicated it and was dropped) and added the general split-root spectral formula as a Mathlib leaf. Reused integral lying-over, finite-dimensional Artinian finiteness, algebraic embeddings, spectral norm existence and absolute-value uniqueness.

Bosch 1.4 Lemma 12 is not in literature/: the report records it as WANTED and proof_origin is agent, so I checked the argument directly instead of against the text. The statement is unchanged and true. I tested it on d=0, c=0, K[ε]/ε² with c=ε, and K×K with c=(0,1). All seven steps are correct. Step 1: descent of the monic divisor through the injective maps C→D and F→D. Step 2: monic division and uniqueness. Step 3: lying-over and Artinian finiteness of C/mC. Steps 4 and 5: lying-over is applied to the injection T[c]⊂C before reduction, and uniqueness of absolute values is applied on the finite extension A/q. Step 6: the embedding C/n→Ω extends the chosen k→Ω. Step 7: the Mathlib leaf applies over the base field k with the spectral norm. The leaf lem-trf-tate-root-spectral-formula is an exact one-line specialization and duplicates no existing node. The new node's UFD clause is used nowhere. I dropped the new node and repointed step 1. Second fix, C1: step 3 relied on integrality of T⊂C that step 1 never established; it now cites lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral. proof_deps was recomputed.
